summary: Additive public-surface change to @cipherstash/stack (minor changeset). Re-exports the existing operation classes from the ./encryption and ./dynamodb subpath entries, adds EncryptedQuery and EncryptedFromSchema type exports to ./types, removes @internal tags from EncryptQueryOperation/BatchEncryptQueryOperation (and their WithLockContext variants), and adds type-only imports plus TSDoc wording fixes. No encryption, payload, lock-context or result-shape logic changes; the encryption/operations <-> encryption/index import cycle already existed at base. The release risk is about API contract, not runtime: runtime class constructors that take internal types become public API, and the ./encryption and ./dynamodb entries now export different classes under the same names. Both are low impact. CI on head passed, but no test checks the exported surface or the built .d.ts files.

behaviour_changes.description: @cipherstash/stack/encryption now exports ten operation classes as runtime values (EncryptOperation, EncryptQueryOperation, BatchEncryptQueryOperation, DecryptOperation, EncryptModelOperation, DecryptModelOperation, BulkEncryptOperation, BulkDecryptOperation, BulkEncryptModelsOperation, BulkDecryptModelsOperation), including their constructors.
@cipherstash/stack/dynamodb now exports its four DynamoDB operation classes as runtime values. Their names match four of the classes exported from ./encryption, but they are different classes.
@cipherstash/stack/types now exports the EncryptedQuery and EncryptedFromSchema types. This is type-only and adds no runtime code.

Removed the @internal TSDoc tags from the EncryptQuery/BatchEncryptQuery operation classes, added type-only imports (LockContext, encryptedTable/Column/Field) so TSDoc links resolve, reworded one @throws line and fixed one @param name. tsconfig has no stripInternal, so @internal did not affect the emitted declarations at base. Type-only imports are erased under verbatimModuleSyntax.
Adds a minor changeset for @cipherstash/stack, so a minor version will be published that includes the widened surface.

failure_scenarios.title: Same-named but different operation classes exported from ./encryption and ./dynamodb
failure_scenarios.trigger: A consumer imports EncryptModelOperation, DecryptModelOperation, BulkEncryptModelsOperation or BulkDecryptModelsOperation from the wrong subpath, for example by IDE auto-import, to type the result of encryptedDynamoDB(...).encryptModel() or EncryptionClient.encryptModel().
failure_scenarios.mechanism: src/encryption/index.ts re-exports the classes from ./operations/* (Client-based constructors). src/dynamodb/index.ts re-exports different classes with the same names from dynamodb/operations/* (EncryptionClient-based constructors). The changeset lists both sets under the same names.
failure_scenarios.consequence: The consumer's code fails to type-check, or instanceof checks against the wrong class return false. This is loud and local; it does not affect encryption or data.
missing_verification: No test or doc distinguishes the two sets of same-named classes.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Note the distinction in the TSDoc/changeset, or alias the DynamoDB exports (for example DynamoDBEncryptModelOperation) before the names ship and become hard to rename.

failure_scenarios.title: Exported constructors and class identity become semver-bound public API
failure_scenarios.trigger: A later release changes an operation constructor (for example its internal FFI Client parameter or its argument order), or a consumer relies on `instanceof EncryptOperation` across package entry points.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: Previously the classes could be reached only as return types. Now they are runtime value exports, so their constructors (which take the internal `Client` type, e.g. encrypt-query.ts constructor) are public. tsup bundles each entry separately. For CJS output, tsup's default of no code splitting would give src/index.ts (which re-exports Encryption) and src/encryption/index.ts separate class copies, so instanceof could fail across entries. This last point comes from tsup defaults and was not verified against built output.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Internal refactors of the operation classes become breaking changes for anyone who constructs them directly, and instanceof checks may misbehave in CJS consumers. The failures are compile-time or logic errors in consumer code, not data or security effects.
missing_verification: No API-surface or built-package (dist) test checks what each subpath exports or how the classes behave across entries.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Document the classes as return types only (not for direct construction or instanceof). Optionally export them type-only (`export type { ... }`), which is enough for naming and TypeDoc links.

verification_gaps.description: Nothing checks the exported surface or the built declaration files. The CI test jobs passed, but they run vitest against source (turbo `test` depends only on ^build). There is no evidence that the stack package's own tsup/dts build ran in CI for this change.

recommended_controls.description: Decide whether the classes should be value exports or type-only exports, and whether the DynamoDB classes need distinct names, before the minor release fixes the names.
Run `pnpm --filter @cipherstash/stack build` and confirm that dist/encryption/index.d.ts, dist/dynamodb/index.d.ts and the CJS bundles expose the new exports.

evidence.claim: Value re-export block of the ten encryption operation classes.
Value re-export block of the four DynamoDB operation classes.
EncryptedQuery and EncryptedFromSchema are added to the type-only exports.
EncryptQueryOperation's constructor takes the internal FFI Client. The module imports noClientError from ../index, a cycle that already existed at base.
The DynamoDB EncryptModelOperation is a separate class whose constructor takes an EncryptionClient, unlike encryption/operations/encrypt-model.ts, which takes a Client.
Only the @internal TSDoc blocks are removed; no logic changes.
verbatimModuleSyntax is true and stripInternal is not set, so the @internal tag did not change emitted declarations and the type-only imports are erased.
Minor changeset for @cipherstash/stack describing the widened exports.
Each subpath entry, including encryption and dynamodb, is built separately as cjs and esm with dts. No splitting option is set.
The ./dynamodb and ./encryption subpaths are published with import/require and types entries.
The change exists so the TypeDoc build in cipherstash/docs can link these symbols. The author reports 0 docs warnings locally.
All 7 check runs on head succeeded (Run Tests on Node 22/24 and Bun, E2E, CodeQL, OSV).
The turbo test task depends on ^build (dependencies' builds) rather than the package's own build.
